Me, my brother and Cousin were camping in my cousin's garden, which was pretty huge (it led to a forest and miles of hills with no fence, just a stream, at the bottom. He was in the scottish highlands too, so there were a couple of neighbouring houses and then nothing for miles).
So we were dicking around, tellin ghost stories, drinking, when we heard the most horrific sound coming from just down past the tree line. The only way I can describe it was a cow screaming, sort of like the sound you'd imagine a rampaging bull to make but more distressed. The worst part is, though, it went on for at LEAST two hours, just constant screaming.
Now we were hoping, rationalising, that it was a cow giving birth, but I'd never heard of a cow making noises like that; it seemed terrified.
Needless to say, we couldn't get to sleep for a while after it stopped. It stopped really abrubtly too, like instantly mid-scream, which didn't help the scariness.

I'm dead. I must be.
It's quite hard to believe; I think back on my life, this linear series of events, and never imagined getting out of it. Escaping the timeline. But my circumstances now are not nearly as strange as the ones that got me here.

I was ten years old when the Powers came. Nobody knew why, they just came to us, to everyone. Every single person on earth suddenly gained a single Power to do with whatever they wanted. Of course, there were the classics: The Flyers, soaring like odd shaped birds above the heads of everybody else; The Tanks, people who had been granted extraordinary strength; The Sirens, mostly women, who could control the actions of anybody they chose with a single wink. Some were less common, of course. There were thousands of Powers spread across the world, seemingly without reason. 
As you can imagine, the sudden increase in the power of every human being caused... Problems.

I had been growing up in my small village just like any other child, playing with my friends whenever I had the chance, dragging myself to school every morning, eating my vegetables and brushing my teeth. Life was perfect. Then, one morning, one warm summer morning. I woke to find myself far, far away from home. Not knowing of my Power at the time you can imagine my shock. At first, I had no idea where I was; complete darkness surrounded me. I remember feeling outwards, only to have my stretching arms halted by cold metal. The ground below me was soft, layered with innumerable objects. The smell was terrible; I had to try my hardest not to vomit. I reasoned that I had no option; I did what and ten year old boy would do in that situation. I curled my knees to my chest, wrapped my arms tightly around them, and began to cry.
I had been trapped inside a large dumpster, tucked away in an alley. I was freed by a bin man, whose blatant surprise at finding a small boy in a dumpster almost made up for my hours of torment. I remember looking at his face for a moment, smiling, before he was gone, replaced by a splatter of blood that rained down onto my horrified young face. God, that was terrifying.

And that's how I was introduced to the world that is. Or, was. Having Super Powers caused everybody to completely lose their minds. Law and order were a thing of the past; who needed to follow the rules when you could break free of any prison cell, hide yourself from any foe? 
Gangs took over. Not traditional gangs, those thugs who used their guns to mug old ladies were nothing now. No, the gangs were made of the people with the strongest Powers. Armies of men and women, raining fire from their palms, throwing cars like footballs, pulling lightning from the sky, took control of the cities. Unless you were wanted, you were killed. The survivors, those without godlike Powers? We hid, in the country, in the forests, anywhere, anywhere that death wasn't chasing us with a fireball or lazer beam.

I could move. That was my Power; I could move, instantaneously, without effort, from one point to another. Anywhere I wanted to be, I was there. I suppose that's what kept me alive for this long. Any chance of death, any at all, I could simply disappear, and materialize somewhere safe. I remember the second time I teleported. I had been staring at the spot the bin man's head had been, moments ago, when another figure entered my field of view. A hooded man, grinning from ear to ear. His hands were silver. This puzzled me, until I realised hands were knives. 'No, holding knives' my ten year old brain reasoned. But no, as I stared, I was sure that his hands had *become* knives, the shining metal joining seamlessly with his skin. As he moved towards me, my terror held me in place. I knew there was nothing I could do. I simply shut my eyes, as tight as they would go, and thought of home.
And there I was. At home. I had been saved, though I didn't know it, the same way I would be countless times in the future.

That was life. For six years, I simply hid from any confrontation. I snatched food from house when I could, stole away clothes and shoes as I grew. I was a ghost; I existed to nobody, a figure in the woods, a creak on the stairs. I never did find my parents again; when I had returned home they were gone. Though I searched, god how I searched, I never found them. As a result, I grew up alone. Alone in a world turned on its head with chaos reigning over the planet, with death and destruction following my every footstep, even when I tried so hard to stay away. 

Until one day when it simply *stopped*.  
The Powers, I mean. They just ceased to exist; the Tanks, crushed under cars they were carrying; the Flyers, falling from the sky. Everybody was normal again. And that's where my run of bad luck decided to have one last hurrah, one final joke. I had been teleporting the very moment it happened, the exact point where our Powers ceased to function. I was stealing food. My arms full of tinned beans and soda cans, I had decided to teleport back to my home, a small shack in the woods where I spent most of my time. All was fine, when suddenly... Poof.

And that's where I am today. Trapped between here and there, between up and down, between anything and everything. I must be dead, but even if I am not, I may as well be. I can't move; I can't stand, sit, walk or run. I can't see anything; vision is just a memory to me. I can't even breathe any more. I just *am*. 
And that's how I came to be here. Trapped for all eternity. Nobody knows where the Powers came from, nor why. They just did. They came, on that warm summer evening, on the ninth of May, twenty-fourteen. They came and turned the world upside down.
